14	Six concrete, transcription-ready sub-questions in service of finally writing the
15	body of `gmScalingP1` (`AlgebraicJacobian/Genus0BaseObjects.lean:457`) and its
16	companion `gmScalingP1_collapse_at_zero` (L472). Verbatim:
17	
18	- **Q1** — exact API of `Proj.affineOpenCoverOfIrrelevantLESpan` specialised to
19	  `f := ![X 0, X 1]` on the standard ℕ-grading of `MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k̄`.
20	- **Q2** — canonical Mathlib path to build
21	  `HomogeneousLocalization.Away (projectiveLineBarGrading kbar) (X i) ≃+*
22	  MvPolynomial Unit kbar`.
23	- **Q3** — chart-side morphism via `pullbackSpecIso`.
24	- **Q4** — cross-chart agreement equation.
25	- **Q5** — `Scheme.Cover.glueMorphisms` signature + how to bridge from
26	  `AffineOpenCover` to `Cover`.
27	- **Q6** — proof body for `gmScalingP1_collapse_at_zero`.
28	
29	## Project artifact(s)
30	
31	- `AlgebraicJacobian/Genus0BaseObjects.lean:457-459` — `def gmScalingP1 := sorry`
32	- `AlgebraicJacobian/Genus0BaseObjects.lean:472-476` — `lemma gmScalingP1_collapse_at_zero := by sorry`
33	- `AlgebraicJacobian/Genus0BaseObjects.lean:268-282` — `zeroPt`/`onePt`/`inftyPt` realisations
34	  (built via `pointOfVec`/`Proj.fromOfGlobalSections`; `zeroPt = pointOfVec (v 0 := 0, v 1 := 1)`,
35	  so `zeroPt` lives in chart `D₊(X 1)`).
36	
37	## Coordinate convention chosen for the rest of this file
38	
39	To avoid confusion between "chart i = D₊(X i)" and "chart i = where X i vanishes",
40	the rest of this document uses the unambiguous version:
41	
42	| Chart name | Open set | Vanishing coord | Affine coord | Where `zeroPt = [0:1]` lives |
43	|---|---|---|---|---|
44	| `chart₀` | `D₊(X 0)` | `X 1 = 0` allowed if `X 0 ≠ 0` | `t := X 1 / X 0` | NO (`X 0 = 0` at zeroPt) |
45	| `chart₁` | `D₊(X 1)` | `X 0 = 0` allowed if `X 1 ≠ 0` | `u := X 0 / X 1` | YES (`u = 0` at zeroPt) |
46	
47	Homogeneous scaling convention picked for `σ_×`:
48	`σ_×([X 0 : X 1], λ) = [λ·X 0 : X 1]` ⇒ `σ_×([0:1], λ) = [0:1] = zeroPt` ∀ λ (✓).
49	This means:
50	
51	- On `chart₁` (where the collapse-at-zero lemma lives): `u ↦ λ·u`, i.e. the ring
52	  map `MvPolynomial Unit k̄ → MvPolynomial Unit k̄ ⊗_{k̄} k̄[λ, λ⁻¹]`, `X () ↦ X () ⊗ λ`.
53	- On `chart₀`: `t = X 1/X 0 ↦ X 1/(λ·X 0) = t/λ`, i.e. `X () ↦ X () ⊗ λ⁻¹`.
54	
55	(The chart-0 map uses `λ⁻¹ ∈ GmRing`, available because GmRing is `Localization.Away (X ())`,
56	so `Localization.Away.invSelf` gives `λ⁻¹`. **This is essential** — the chart-0 map only
57	makes sense after tensor with Gm precisely because that's what makes `λ⁻¹` available.)
58

60	
61	All citations are to the lake-checked-out Mathlib in
62	`.lake/packages/mathlib/Mathlib/`. Line numbers are from current files at iter-168.

64	- **`AlgebraicGeometry.Proj.affineOpenCoverOfIrrelevantLESpan`**
65	  (`AlgebraicGeometry/ProjectiveSpectrum/Basic.lean:324-335`) — verbatim signature:
66	
67	  ```lean
68	  noncomputable
69	  def affineOpenCoverOfIrrelevantLESpan {ι : Type*} (f : ι → A) {m : ι → ℕ}
70	      (f_deg : ∀ i, f i ∈ 𝒜 (m i)) (hm : ∀ i, 0 < m i)
71	      (hf : (HomogeneousIdeal.irrelevant 𝒜).toIdeal ≤ Ideal.span (Set.range f)) :
72	      (Proj 𝒜).AffineOpenCover where
73	    I₀ := ι
74	    X i := .of (Away 𝒜 (f i))
75	    f i := awayι 𝒜 (f i) (f_deg i) (hm i)
76	    idx x := (mem_iSup.mp ((iSup_basicOpen_eq_top 𝒜 f hf).ge (Set.mem_univ x))).choose
77	    covers x := ⟨_, _⟩
78	  ```
79	
80	  Where `Away 𝒜 f := HomogeneousLocalization 𝒜 (Submonoid.powers f)`
81	  (`RingTheory/GradedAlgebra/HomogeneousLocalization.lean:601`) and
82	  `Proj.awayι 𝒜 f f_deg hm : Spec (.of <| Away 𝒜 f) ⟶ Proj 𝒜`
83	  (`AlgebraicGeometry/ProjectiveSpectrum/Basic.lean:189`).
84	
85	- **`Scheme.AffineOpenCover`** (`AlgebraicGeometry/Cover/Open.lean:118-119`):
86	  `abbrev AffineOpenCover := AffineCover @IsOpenImmersion`.
87	- **`AffineCover` (with `cover` field)** (`AlgebraicGeometry/Cover/MorphismProperty.lean:193-218`):
88	  ```lean
89	  structure AffineCover (P : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) where
90	    I₀ : Type v ; X : I₀ → CommRingCat.{u} ; f : ∀ j, Spec (X j) ⟶ S
91	    idx : S → I₀ ; covers : ∀ x, x ∈ Set.range (f (idx x))
92	    map_prop (j) : P (f j) := by infer_instance
93	  def AffineCover.cover : X.AffineCover P → X.Cover (precoverage P) := ...
94	  ```
95	  `AffineOpenCover.openCover` is a `simps`-generated alias for `.cover`
96	  (`Cover/Open.lean:128`).
97	
98	- **`Scheme.Cover.glueMorphisms`** (`AlgebraicGeometry/Gluing.lean:436-445`) —
99	  verbatim signature:
100	  ```lean
101	  def glueMorphisms (𝒰 : OpenCover.{v} X) {Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : ∀ x, 𝒰.X x ⟶ Y)
102	      (hf : ∀ x y, pullback.fst (𝒰.f x) (𝒰.f y) ≫ f x =
103	                    pullback.snd _ _ ≫ f y) :
104	      X ⟶ Y
105	  theorem ι_glueMorphisms ... (𝒰.f x ≫ 𝒰.glueMorphisms f hf = f x)  -- L457
106	  theorem hom_ext ... (∀ x, 𝒰.f x ≫ f₁ = 𝒰.f x ≫ f₂) → f₁ = f₂      -- L448
107	  ```
108	  Takes an `OpenCover`, not an `AffineOpenCover`. Bridge via
109	  `AffineOpenCover.openCover`.
110	
111	- **`AlgebraicGeometry.pullbackSpecIso`**
112	  (`AlgebraicGeometry/Pullbacks.lean:703-708`) — verbatim signature:

64

Witness for "for each chart W of A, `f^# ∘ iterateFrobenius_{Γ(W), p, n} = iterateFrobenius_{Γ(f^{-1}W), p, n} ∘ f^#`" — gives chart-by-chart Frobenius iteration as a direct ring-level RingHom-commutation, no scheme-level lift needed |

73	
74	The iter-143 d_app type-coercion obstacle is **structurally
75	reproducible** in piece (iii) sub-piece 2 (restriction compatibility):
76	both require `Pushforward.comp_eq` (definitional rfl) chained with
77	propositional-only `≫ = ` to bridge composite Hom equalities. The
78	chart-algebra route uses `pullbackSpecIso` + ring-level
79	`iterateFrobenius` instead, **completely avoiding pushforward-
80	composite Eq.mpr/eqToHom transport**.
81	
82	## Decisions identified
83	
84	### Decision 1: Does iter-143 d_app type-coercion foreshadow piece (iii) scheme-Frobenius type-coercion cost?
85	
86	The iter-143 d_app obstacle is the chain:
87	
88	  `(fst).left ≫ G.hom = (snd).left ≫ G.hom`   (propositional, via `(fst).w` + `(snd).w`)
89	   → `Pushforward.comp_eq` for both sides (definitional rfl)
90	   → `Adjunction.homEquiv_naturality_right_symm` transpose (modulo type alignment via `eqToHom`)
91	   → equating two natural transformations with different
92	     codomain pushforward parametrisations.
93	
94	The iter-143 prover task-result is explicit: "the recipe is correct;
95	the difficulty is at the **Lean-level type-coercion**, NOT at the
96	recipe level. This is a **tooling-level obstacle, not a mathematical
97	one**."
98	
99	**Piece (iii) scheme-Frobenius sub-piece-by-sub-piece foreshadow audit:**
100	
101	- **Sub-piece 1** (`Scheme.absoluteFrobenius` definition, ~150–300 LOC):
102	  builds an `LRS.Hom X X` from `base = 𝟙` + sheaf-NatTrans (per-open
103	  `frobenius`) + stalk-locality. **Single Hom on X**, NOT a
104	  composition of two scheme morphisms. **No pushforward-composite
105	  obstacle**. Sub-piece 1 does NOT foreshadow the iter-143 obstacle.
106	
107	- **Sub-piece 2** (restriction compatibility `F_X |_U = F_U`,
108	  ~80–150 LOC): commuting square `U.ι ≫ F_X = F_U ≫ U.ι` via
109	  `Scheme.Hom.ext` + per-open `frobenius_comm`. **Same shape** as
110	  iter-143 d_app pushforward-composite chase: one side is `U.ι ≫ F_X`
111	  (composition); proof goes through `comp_c_app` + naturality. **Sub-
112	  piece 2 DOES foreshadow** the iter-143 obstacle.
113	
114	  However, sub-piece 2's commuting square is **easier**: `U.ι` is an
115	  open inclusion (much simpler than the binary-product `(fst).left`/
116	  `(snd).left` chase; `U.ι` has a controlled `(Opens.map U.ι.base)`-
117	  preimage with definitional `IsOpenImmersion` API). The iter-141
118	  ~80–150 LOC estimate is plausible **modulo** a ~20–40% Eq.mpr/
119	  eqToHom tax that compounds (per iter-143 evidence). Effective range
120	  ~96–210 LOC.

1	# Analogy: Mathlib LOC cost of M3 — building a positive-genus `JacobianWitness`
2	
3	## Slug
4	m3-route-audit
5	
6	## Iteration
7	123
8	
9	## Question
10	
11	For an arbitrary smooth proper geometrically irreducible curve `C` over a
12	field `k` with `genus C ≥ 1`, what is the cumulative LOC of upstream
13	Mathlib work the project would need to contribute (or backfill in-tree)
14	in order to discharge the existential `positiveGenusWitness` —
15	equivalently, the higher-genus case of `nonempty_jacobianWitness`
16	(`AlgebraicJacobian/Jacobian.lean:176`)?
17	
18	The question is asked over two prescribed construction routes (FGA via
19	Picard, and symmetric-power via Stein factorisation), with a tiebreaker
20	on cross-utility for general Mathlib AG infrastructure, and a hard
21	escalation rule at the 5000-LOC mark.
22	
23	## Project artifact(s)
24	- `AlgebraicJacobian/Jacobian.lean:143-179` — `JacobianWitness` bundled
25	  structure and `nonempty_jacobianWitness` sorry, the M3 target.
26	- `AlgebraicJacobian/Jacobian.lean:49-114` — `IsAlbanese` predicate and
27	  `IsAlbanese.unique` (positive-genus need only the existence of one
28	  Albanese witness).
29	- `AlgebraicJacobian/Genus.lean:65-68` — the project's working definition
30	  `genus C := Module.finrank k (H¹(C, O_C))`, which constrains Route B's
31	  RR formulation.
32	
33	## Mathlib snapshot used
34	
35	Mathlib package shipped with this project's lake manifest (b80f227
36	neighbourhood). Concretely:
37	
38	- `AlgebraicGeometry/` directory contents: `AffineScheme`, `AffineSpace`,
39	  `EllipticCurve/{Affine,DivisionPolynomial,Jacobian,Projective}`,
40	  `Geometrically/{Connected,Integral,Irreducible}`, `Group/{Abelian,Smooth}`,
41	  `IdealSheaf`, `Modules/{Presheaf,Sheaf,Tilde}`,
42	  `Morphisms/{Affine,…,Proper,QuasiCompact,…,Smooth,SmoothFiber,…}`,
43	  `ProjectiveSpectrum`, `Sites/{BigZariski,…,Representability,Etale,Fpqc}`,
44	  `ZariskisMainTheorem`, `ValuativeCriterion`.
45	- Searches verified the **absence** of: `PicardScheme`, `PicardFunctor`,
46	  `HilbertScheme`, `HilbertFunctor`, `QuotScheme`, `QuotFunctor`,
47	  `SymmetricPower` on schemes, `Scheme.action` / scheme-level group
48	  action, `Scheme` quotient by a finite group, `RiemannRoch`, Cartier or
49	  Weil divisor on a general scheme (`EllipticCurve.Jacobian` is the
50	  Weierstrass model, not a general divisor theory), `BrillNoether`,
51	  `SteinFactorization`, `RelativeSpec` / `Spec_Y` of a quasi-coherent
52	  algebra, `R^if_*` higher direct image, `Functor.Monoidal` on
53	  `SheafOfModules.pullback`, and `Module.Invertible` lifted to sheaves.
54	
55	What **does** exist (relevant partials):
56	
57	- `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalRepresentability.isRepresentable`
58	  (`Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Sites.Representability:201-203`): the general
59	  "locally representable Zariski sheaf is representable" tool (Stacks 01JJ).
60	  Both routes consume this once they have produced their local data.
61	- `AlgebraicGeometry.isCommMonObj_of_isProper_of_geometricallyIntegral`
62	  (`Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Group.Abelian:128-144`, tag 0BFD):
63	  proper geometrically integral group scheme over a field is commutative.
64	- `AlgebraicGeometry.smooth_of_grpObj_of_isAlgClosed`
65	  (`Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Group.Smooth:38`): reduced locally-of-finite-type
66	  group scheme over algebraically closed `k` is smooth — usable to upgrade
67	  smoothness of the candidate Jacobian after geometric base change.
68	- `AlgebraicGeometry.finite_appTop_of_universallyClosed`
69	  (`Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.Proper:154`): the **0-th case** of
70	  Stein factorisation — `Γ(X, ⊤)` is finite over `K` for integral
71	  universally closed `X / Spec K`.
72	- `AlgebraicGeometry.Flat`
73	  (`Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.Flat`) — flat morphisms exist as a
74	  class; sheaf-of-modules flatness does not.
75	- `SheafOfModules.Presentation` and `Presentation.IsFinite`
76	  (`Mathlib.Algebra.Category.ModuleCat.Sheaf.Quasicoherent:44-57`):
77	  finite presentations of sheaves of modules over a general ringed site;
78	  the abstract notion is in place but it is **not lifted to a typeclass
79	  `QuasiCoherent` / `IsCoherent` on `SheafOfModules`** in the form Stacks
80	  03DL or 01BD specify, nor is there a `Scheme.QuasiCoherent` or
81	  `Scheme.IsCoherent` namespace.
82	- `Subgroup.connectedComponentOfOne`
83	  (`Mathlib.Topology.Algebra.Group.Basic:740`): identity-component as a
84	  `Subgroup` for **topological** groups; **no** scheme-level analog
85	  (i.e. no reduced closed subgroup-scheme structure on `G^0 ⊆ G` for a
86	  locally-of-finite-type `k`-group scheme).
87	- `CommRing.Pic` (`Mathlib.RingTheory.PicardGroup:407-408`): ring-level
88	  Picard *group* via `Shrink (Skeleton (SemimoduleCat R))ˣ`. The scheme
89	  analog is the project's `AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/*` (post-iter-109),
90	  **not** Mathlib's. There is no Picard *scheme* in either place.
91	
92	## Decisions identified
93	
94	Per the directive the "decision" surface is "which of the two strategy
95	routes does the project pick?", decomposed into a per-piece LOC count
96	plus tiebreakers. The structure below follows that.
97	
98	### Route A — Picard scheme via FGA
99	
100	#### Piece A1: Hilbert scheme representability for projective schemes

1	# Analogy: minimal hypotheses for open-immersion Beck–Chevalley + does [IsAffine V] collapse its core to the affine brick
2	
3	## Mode
4	api-alignment
5	
6	## Slug
7	fbc329
8	
9	## Iteration
10	329
11	
12	## Question
13	(1) Is `openImmersion_beckChevalley` (currently arbitrary `F`, no `hF`, no qc) sound/provable for
14	arbitrary `F`, and what is the minimal correct hypothesis set? (2) Does `[IsAffine V]` collapse the
15	per-affine member node `lem:openimm_bareBC_app_isIso_affine` DIRECTLY to the sorry-free affine brick
16	`affinePushforwardPullbackBaseChange`, vs. re-deriving the tilde matching by hand (the no-affine
17	fbc327 route)?
18	
19	## Project artifact(s)
20	- `Cohomology/CechHigherDirectImageUnconditional.lean:914` `openImmersion_beckChevalley` — arbitrary-`F` signature; STAGE-2 sorry = `IsIso (bareBC.app (p^*F))`.
21	- `:832` `openImmersion_bareBC`; `:872` `isOpenImmersion_of_isPullback_left`; `:948` `twisted_cech_nerve_per_sigma` (consumer).
22	- `:386` `pullback_isQuasicoherent` (hF-gated); `:398` `pullbackRestrict_iso_tilde` (hF-gated); `:422` `pushPullObj_pushforward_iso_tilde` (hF-gated).
23	- `:487` `coverInterOpen_isAffine` (V=U_σ affine from `[IsSeparated f]`+`[IsAffine S]`+affine cover); `:520` `restrictedCartesianAffinePushout`.
24	- `FlatBaseChange.lean:798` `affinePushforwardPullbackBaseChange` (sorry-free brick = `pullback_spec_tilde_iso` + `pushforward_spec_tilde_iso` + `cancelBaseChange`); `:875` `flatBaseChange_pushforward_isIso` (pushforward-qcoh needs `[QuasiCompact f][QuasiSeparated f]`).
25	- `ModulesCoverConservativity.lean:37` `isIso_iff_isIso_restrict` (iter-328 keystone, cover-localization of IsIso).
26	- `analogies/fbc327.md` (the base-free no-affine cover-refinement route).
27	
28	## Decisions identified
29	
30	### Decision 1: minimal hypotheses for `openImmersion_beckChevalley`
31	- **Mathematics**: the map is `g'^* p_* F → p'_* gV^* F` for `p` an open immersion (= flat) and `g'`
32	  arbitrary. This is FLAT BASE CHANGE (Stacks 02KH/02KG). The outer `g'^*` is sheafification of the
33	  presheaf tensor `(p_*F)(U) ⊗_{O(U)} O'(W)`; that tensor description only matches `p'_* gV^* F`
34	  sections when the sheaf is QUASI-COHERENT. For a general `O_X`-module the comparison FAILS. ⇒ the
35	  arbitrary-`F` signature is UNSOUND / not provable; `hF : F.IsQuasicoherent` is required.
36	- **`[QuasiCompact p]`**: the blueprint hand route (`lem:openimm_pushforward_qcoh_tilde`) presents the
37	  GLOBAL `p_* p^* F` as `Ñ` over an affine `U`, which needs `p_* p^* F` quasicoherent. Pushforward
38	  preserves qcoh only under qcqs (Stacks 01XJ; project's only such lemma is `flatBaseChange_pushforward_isIso`,
39	  gated `[QuasiCompact f][QuasiSeparated f]`; `pushforward_iso_preserves_qcoh` handles ONLY isos).
40	  Open immersions are always quasi-SEPARATED but NOT quasi-compact (the blueprint proof's claim "an
41	  open immersion is quasi-compact" is a soundness gap — true only when `V` is retrocompact, e.g. `V`
42	  affine + `X` quasi-separated). So the HAND route silently needs `[QuasiCompact p]`. The BRICK route
43	  (Decision 2) does NOT: it pushes forward affine-local tildes, never forming the global `p_* p^* F`,
44	  and pushforward of a tilde along a `Spec`-map is qcoh by construction. ⇒ with the brick route only
45	  `hF` is needed.
46	- **Sibling alignment**: `pullback_isQuasicoherent`, `pullbackRestrict_iso_tilde`,
47	  `pushPullObj_pushforward_iso_tilde` are ALL `hF`-gated. `openImmersion_beckChevalley` is the lone
48	  `hF`-free outlier in the tilde family.
49	- **Gap**: divergent-and-wrong (the arbitrary-`F` statement is false).
50	- **Verdict**: ALIGN_WITH_MATHLIB — re-sign with `hF : F.IsQuasicoherent`. Do NOT add `[QuasiCompact p]`
51	  (avoidable via brick route). The lemma is not frozen in `archon-protected.yaml`, so the re-sign is allowed.
52	
53	### Decision 2: does `[IsAffine V]` collapse the member node to the affine brick?
54	- **The collapse (YES, for the per-affine member node)**: check `IsIso bareBC` over an affine cover
55	  `{W_j = Spec B}` of `X'` refining `(g')⁻¹(affine opens of X)`, so `g'(W_j) ⊆ U_j = Spec A`. With
56	  `V` affine and `X` separated (affine diagonal), `V ∩ U_j` is affine `= Spec A'`, and the restricted
57	  square over `(W_j, U_j)`
58	  ```
59	    W_j ×_{U_j}(V∩U_j) --→ V∩U_j
60	        |                    | (open immersion = Spec(A→A'))
61	        v                    v
62	       W_j  ----Spec ψ---→  U_j
63	  ```
64	  is a FULLY-AFFINE pushout square. `openimm_bareBC_app_isIso_affine` over `W_j` is then EXACTLY
65	  `affinePushforwardPullbackBaseChange` with `f = Spec(A→A')` (the open immersion `V∩U_j↪U_j`) and
66	  `M = Γ(V∩U_j, p^*F)` (an `A'`-module, presented because `p^*F = F|_V` is qcoh from `hF`). The brick
67	  ALREADY packages `pullback_spec_tilde_iso + pushforward_spec_tilde_iso + cancelBaseChange`, so it
68	  REPLACES the three hand leaves `openimm_outer_pullback_affine_tensor` / `openimm_pushforward_sections_basechange`
69	  / the cancelBaseChange-matching with ONE brick call. Crucial subtlety: pushforward of `p^*F` along
70	  `p` and restriction-to-`U_j` commute for ARBITRARY sheaves (just `(p_*G)|_{U_j} = (V∩U_j↪U_j)_*(G|_{V∩U_j})`,
71	  the open-restriction/`pushforward_obj_obj` identity), so the brick never needs `p_*p^*F` qcoh ⇒ no qc.
72	- **What `[IsAffine V]` does NOT do**: it does NOT make `openImmersion_beckChevalley` an affine-brick
73	  one-liner. `X'` is still NON-affine, so the brick (affine target) cannot apply to the X'-level square;
74	  you STILL need the iter-328 keystone `isIso_iff_isIso_restrict` to localize the X'-level `IsIso` to
75	  the `W_j`, plus the refining affine cover (`openImmersion_refiningAffineCover`, NOT yet built — pull
76	  the standard affine cover of `X` back along `g'`, refine each preimage by its own affine cover), plus
77	  the per-`W_j` local-square construction (an analog of `restrictedCartesianAffinePushout` over `W_j`
78	  with `V∩U_j`, distinct from the existing global S-affine one). In the CONSUMER the refining cover is
79	  free: the base-changed cover `𝒰'` is already affine with `g'(𝒰'_i)⊆𝒰_i` affine.
80	- **vs. fbc327 no-affine route**: fbc327 builds the SAME per-`W_j` tensor matching (cancelBaseChange
81	  for the local square) BY HAND without the brick — over-general and re-derives what the brick packages.
82	- **Gap**: divergent-with-cost (fbc327 route is the costlier sibling of the brick route).
83	- **Verdict**: DIVERGE_INTENTIONALLY from fbc327's hand-matching → use the affine-V brick route. It is
84	  materially cheaper (one sorry-free brick call per member vs. 3 hand leaves), at the cost of `hF` +
85	  `[IsAffine V]` + X-separatedness threading.
86	
87	## Threading cost (re-sign scope)
88	- `openImmersion_beckChevalley` (:914): add `(hF : F.IsQuasicoherent)`, `[IsAffine V]`, and an
89	  X-separatedness witness for `V∩U_j` affine (e.g. `[IsSeparated (terminal.from X)]`, or thread the
90	  base datum so it is derivable). NOT frozen → allowed.
91	- `twisted_cech_nerve_per_sigma` (:948): add `hF`, `[IsAffine S]`, `[∀ i, IsAffine (𝒰.X i)]`,
92	  `[Nonempty κ]` so `coverInterOpen_isAffine` supplies `[IsAffine V]` and separatedness (`[IsSeparated f]`
93	  already present).
94	- `twisted_cech_nerve_iso` (:991): already carries cover-affineness `[∀ i, IsAffine (𝒰.X i)]`; ADD
95	  `hF` and `[IsAffine S]`, thread to the per-σ leaf.
96	- `cechComplex_baseChange_cosimplicialIso` (:1047): TERMINAL — already has `[IsAffine S]`,
97	  `[IsAffine S']`, `hF`. No change. (And `cechComplex_baseChange_iso` :1089 likewise has `hF`.)
98	- So the thread is short: cosimplicialIso (has all) → twisted_cech_nerve_iso (+hF,+IsAffine S) →
99	  twisted_cech_nerve_per_sigma (+hF,+IsAffine S,+cover-affine,+Nonempty) → openImmersion_beckChevalley
100	  (+hF,+IsAffine V,+X-separated).
101	
102	## Recommendation
103	ALIGN: re-sign `openImmersion_beckChevalley` with `hF : F.IsQuasicoherent` (the arbitrary-`F` form is
104	unsound — flat base change fails off the qcoh locus) and `[IsAffine V]` (+ X-separatedness). Prove it
105	via the iter-328 keystone `isIso_iff_isIso_restrict` over a refining affine cover `{W_j}` of `X'`,
106	discharging each member with `affinePushforwardPullbackBaseChange` on the local fully-affine pushout
107	square (`f = Spec(A→A')` for `V∩U_j↪U_j`, `M = Γ(V∩U_j, p^*F)`). This REPLACES the effort-broken hand
108	leaves `openimm_outer_pullback_affine_tensor` / `openimm_pushforward_sections_basechange` /
109	`openimm_bareBC_app_isIso_affine`-via-cancelBaseChange with one sorry-free brick call per member, and
110	AVOIDS `[QuasiCompact p]` (the brick never forms the global `p_*p^*F`). The remaining net-new work is
111	`openImmersion_refiningAffineCover` (pull std affine cover of X back along g', refine — Mathlib
112	ingredients only; in the consumer it is the existing `𝒰'`) and the per-`W_j` local affine pushout
113	square. fbc327's no-affine route is over-general and should be retired in favour of this. Related:
114	[[fbc327]], [[fbc-keystone-landed-328]], [[fbc-affine-bridge-325]], [[fbc-isiso-barebc-327]].

1	# Analogy: Carrier shape for `Pic0Scheme / PicScheme / QuotScheme / picSharp / ...`
2	
3	## Mode
4	api-alignment
5	
6	## Slug
7	carrier-soundness-design
8	
9	## Iteration
10	195
11	
12	## Question
13	
14	The project has 7+ load-bearing typed `:= sorry` definition carriers
15	(`PicScheme`, `Pic0Scheme`, `QuotScheme`, `picSharp`, `divFunctor`,
16	`abelMap`, `PicSharp / presheaf / etSheaf`, `addCommGroup`) whose
17	sorries propagate silently through typeclass synthesis. Which of the
18	three proposed carrier shapes — A (existential + `Classical.choose`),
19	B (opaque + axiom), or C (structure-of-data) — is the Mathlib idiom,
20	and which actually delivers kernel-only-axiom downstream consumers?
21	
22	## Project artifact(s)
23	
24	- `AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean:132` — `picSharp := sorry`
25	  (forward-reference functor stub).
26	- `AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean:147` — `divFunctor := sorry`
27	  (same).
28	- `AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean:187` — `PicScheme := sorry`
29	  (carrier of the FGA representability theorem).
30	- `AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean:226` — `abelMap := sorry`
31	  (natural transformation stub).
32	- `AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean:324` — `representable := sorry`
33	  (the `RepresentableBy` witness).
34	- `AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/IdentityComponent.lean:738` — `Pic0Scheme := sorry`
35	  (the identity component, body intended to be
36	  `GroupScheme.IdentityComponent (PicScheme C)`).
37	- `AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/QuotScheme.lean:326` — `QuotScheme := sorry`
38	  (theorem-shaped: `∃ Q, Nonempty (RepresentableBy Q)`).
39	- `AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/RelPicFunctor.lean:205, 284, 323, 370, 429, 478` —
40	  `addCommGroup`, `PicSharp`, `PicSharp.functorial`, `presheaf`,
41	  `etSheaf`, `etSheafUnit` (functor / instance / sheaf assembly stubs).
42	
43	## Decisions identified
44	
45	### Decision: How to encode a carrier whose existence is proved by a
46	deep theorem (FGA / Kleiman §4) but whose body must be available NOW
47	for downstream typeclass synthesis
48	
49	- **Mathlib idiom**: a Prop-valued typeclass packaging the existence
50	  claim, plus a `noncomputable def` extracting the carrier via
51	  `Classical.choose` of the typeclass instance. Concretely
52	  `CategoryTheory.Functor.IsRepresentable` + `Functor.reprX`:
53	
54	  ```lean
55	  -- Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Yoneda
56	  class Functor.IsRepresentable (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v) : Prop where
57	    has_representation : ∃ Y, Nonempty (F.RepresentableBy Y)
58	
59	  noncomputable def Functor.reprX (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v) [hF : F.IsRepresentable] : C :=
60	    hF.has_representation.choose
61	  ```
62	
63	  Empirically `#print axioms Functor.reprX` reports
64	  `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]` — exactly the kernel-only
65	  axiom set the project targets.
66	
67	  Why Mathlib chose this: separating *existence* (a `Prop` typeclass,
68	  proved separately and possibly conditionally) from *extraction*
69	  (`Classical.choose` is kernel-only) lets downstream lemmas take the
70	  typeclass as a parameter and remain kernel-clean. The Mathlib
71	  source for `Functor.RepresentableBy` keeps the data structure
72	  separate from the existence claim — that is the load-bearing split.
73	
74	- **Project's current path**: `PicScheme C := sorry` (a typed
75	  carrier-level sorry) plus a separate `representable C : ... := sorry`
76	  theorem. Downstream lemmas reference `PicScheme C` directly, so
77	  every instance / theorem about `PicScheme C` transitively depends on
78	  `sorryAx` through the carrier.
79	
80	- **Gap**: divergent-and-wrong (in the kernel-axiom-soundness sense).
81	  Mathlib never writes `def MyType := sorry` for a carrier; it always
82	  either (a) constructs concretely (`SplittingField`,
83	  `AlgebraicClosure`, `Localization`, `UniformSpace.Completion`,
84	  `presheafToSheaf`), or (b) parameterizes by an existence typeclass
85	  and extracts via `Classical.choose` (`Functor.reprX`,
86	  `Limits.getColimitCocone`).
87	
88	- **Cost of divergence**: silent `sorryAx` propagation through every
89	  typeclass synthesis touching `PicScheme C` / `Pic0Scheme C` /
90	  `QuotScheme`. `lean_verify` on the protected `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian`

33	  presheaf tensor `(p_*F)(U) ⊗_{O(U)} O'(W)`; that tensor description only matches `p'_* gV^* F`

37	  GLOBAL `p_* p^* F` as `Ñ` over an affine `U`, which needs `p_* p^* F` quasicoherent. Pushforward
38	  preserves qcoh only under qcqs (Stacks 01XJ; project's only such lemma is `flatBaseChange_pushforward_isIso`,
39	  gated `[QuasiCompact f][QuasiSeparated f]`; `pushforward_iso_preserves_qcoh` handles ONLY isos).
40	  Open immersions are always quasi-SEPARATED but NOT quasi-compact (the blueprint proof's claim "an

42	  affine + `X` quasi-separated). So the HAND route silently needs `[QuasiCompact p]`. The BRICK route
43	  (Decision 2) does NOT: it pushes forward affine-local tildes, never forming the global `p_* p^* F`,

45	  `hF` is needed.

47	  `pushPullObj_pushforward_iso_tilde` are ALL `hF`-gated. `openImmersion_beckChevalley` is the lone

50	- **Verdict**: ALIGN_WITH_MATHLIB — re-sign with `hF : F.IsQuasicoherent`. Do NOT add `[QuasiCompact p]`

56	  `V` affine and `X` separated (affine diagonal), `V ∩ U_j` is affine `= Spec A'`, and the restricted

70	  `p` and restriction-to-`U_j` commute for ARBITRARY sheaves (just `(p_*G)|_{U_j} = (V∩U_j↪U_j)_*(G|_{V∩U_j})`,
71	  the open-restriction/`pushforward_obj_obj` identity), so the brick never needs `p_*p^*F` qcoh ⇒ no qc.
72	- **What `[IsAffine V]` does NOT do**: it does NOT make `openImmersion_beckChevalley` an affine-brick
73	  one-liner. `X'` is still NON-affine, so the brick (affine target) cannot apply to the X'-level square;
74	  you STILL need the iter-328 keystone `isIso_iff_isIso_restrict` to localize the X'-level `IsIso` to

2	
3	## Mode
4	api-alignment
5	
6	## Slug
7	ts-design206
8	
9	## Iteration
10	206
11	
12	## Question
13	To equip the relative Picard functor with its `AddCommGroup` (the group law
14	"tensor of line bundles") the project is building the FULL symmetric monoidal
15	category `Scheme.Modules X` (= `sheafification ∘ PresheafOfModules.Monoidal.tensorObj`),
16	which has bottomed out in the verified-absent `MonoidalClosed (PresheafOfModules R₀)`
17	(needed for the `whiskerLeft` stability of the localizing morphism property).
18	Is the full `MonoidalCategory (Scheme.Modules X)` the right Mathlib-aligned shape
19	for obtaining only the group law on LINE BUNDLES, or does Mathlib have a lighter
20	idiom that yields the `AddCommGroup` on line-bundle iso-classes WITHOUT the full
21	monoidal (let alone monoidal-closed) structure on all modules?
22	
23	## Project artifact(s)
24	- `AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/TensorObjSubstrate.lean`:113–152 — `Scheme.Modules.tensorObj`
25	  and the `monoidalCategory : MonoidalCategory X.Modules` instance (`:= sorry`).
26	- `TensorObjSubstrate.lean`:249–304 — `tensorObj_restrict_iso`, `tensorObj_isLocallyTrivial`,
27	  `exists_tensorObj_inverse` (the line-bundle cone).
28	- `TensorObjSubstrate.lean`:399–454 — `isMonoidal_W_of_whiskerLeft` /
29	  `monoidalCategoryOfIsMonoidalW`: the transport reducing the whole substrate to the
30	  lone `whiskerLeft` fact `W g → W (F ◁ g)` for ALL `F`.
31	- `RelPicFunctor.lean`:235–269 — the `addCommGroup` sorry the cone discharges.
32	- `LineBundlePullback.lean`:115–131 — `IsLocallyTrivial` (the project's self-described
33	  "stand-in for the missing Mathlib `IsInvertible` predicate") and `OnProduct` carrier.
34	
35	## Decisions identified
36	
37	### Decision A: full `MonoidalCategory (Scheme.Modules X)` (→ `MonoidalClosed (PresheafOfModules R₀)`) as the substrate for the group law
38	
39	- **Mathlib idiom**. Mathlib's Picard group is `CommRing.Pic R := Shrink (Skeleton (SemimoduleCat R))ˣ`
40	  with the `CommGroup` transported from `Units` of the skeleton `CommMonoid`
41	  (`Mathlib.RingTheory.PicardGroup`, `CommRing.Pic` def:407, `instCommGroupPic`:412;
42	  `CategoryTheory.Skeleton.instCommMonoid` from `Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Skeleton`).
43	  The invertibility carrier is a **Prop predicate** `Module.Invertible R M`
44	  (PicardGroup.lean:78), NOT a bundled monoidal object. Crucially the monoidal
45	  category underlying the skeleton there is `ModuleCat R` over a **fixed** ring
46	  (`ModuleCat.monoidalCategory`, `ModuleCat.MonoidalCategory.symmetricCategory`,
47	  `Mathlib.Algebra.Category.ModuleCat.Monoidal.{Basic,Symmetric}`) — which needs **no**
48	  sheafification, localization, or `MonoidalClosed`.
49	- **Project's path**. Build `MonoidalCategory` on ALL quasi-coherent modules
50	  `Scheme.Modules X`, whose only remaining gap is `whiskerLeft : W g → W (F ◁ g)`
51	  for an ARBITRARY presheaf-of-modules `F`, provable (à la Mathlib's
52	  `GrothendieckTopology.W.whiskerLeft`) only through `MonoidalClosed (PresheafOfModules R₀)`
53	  — verified absent and a multi-file Mathlib-PR-scale build.
54	- **Gap**: divergent-with-cost (over-building). The consumer (`RelPicFunctor`
55	  `addCommGroup`) only ever tensors **line bundles** (`IsLocallyTrivial`, locally free
56	  rank 1). Line bundles are **flat** — in Mathlib, `Module.Invertible R M` already
57	  yields `instance : Module.Finite`, `instance : Projective` (PicardGroup.lean:195–196),
58	  hence flat. For a FLAT `F`, `F ◁ g` is locally bijective whenever `g` is, by ordinary
59	  exactness: flat ⇒ `lTensor` preserves injectivity
60	  (`Module.Flat.lTensor_preserves_injective_linearMap`, used in PicardGroup.lean:205–207;
61	  packaged as `Module.Invertible.lTensor_bijective_iff`, PicardGroup.lean:223–229), and
62	  `⊗` is always right-exact so it preserves surjectivity. So the ENTIRE reason the project
63	  needs `MonoidalClosed` — that `whiskerLeft` is false elementwise for non-flat `F` — evaporates
64	  once the scope is the flat/line-bundle subcategory. The directive's "elementwise exactness
65	  (needs flatness)" dead-end was a dead-end ONLY because the target was all modules; the
66	  flatness it "needs" is automatic for line bundles.
67	- **Cost of divergence**: a verified-absent multi-file `MonoidalClosed (PresheafOfModules R₀)`
68	  build (the relative internal hom over a varying base ring; the module analogue of
69	  `Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Sites.Monoidal`), to obtain coherence (pentagon/triangle/hexagon
70	  + monoidal-closedness) that the group law never consumes — the group axioms on iso-classes
71	  are *propositions* (`Nonempty (… ≅ …)`), insensitive to coherence.
72	- **Verdict**: ALIGN_WITH_MATHLIB — abandon the all-modules monoidal-closed route; build the
73	  group law on the line-bundle (flat) subcategory, where `whiskerLeft`/`tensorObj_restrict_iso`
74	  reduce to elementary flat-exactness already in Mathlib.
75	
76	### Decision B: shape of the group-law assembly (`addCommGroup_via_tensorObj` hand-roll vs `Units ∘ Skeleton` + invertibility predicate)
77	
78	- **Mathlib idiom**. `Pic = Units (Skeleton C)` for a braided monoidal `C`
79	  (`CommRing.Pic`, `instCommGroupPic`); the iso-class arithmetic is the family
80	  `Pic.mk_tensor` ([M⊗N]=[M]·[N]), `Pic.mk_dual` ([Mᵛ]=[M]⁻¹), `mul_eq_tensor`,

74	    {X : Scheme} {M N : X.Modules} (φ : M ⟶ N) (𝒰 : X.OpenCover) :

12	## Question

14	What is the Mathlib-idiomatic way to make the two interchangeable at the NatTrans/whisker level
15	WITHOUT a global isDefEq blowup, and how does Mathlib prove `leftAdjointUniq`/`conjugateEquiv`
16	comparison cocycles over adjoint functors written two ways without the monolithic functor isDefEq?

23	`Scheme.Modules.pullback` is **NOT project-local**. It is **Mathlib**:
24	`Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Modules/Sheaf.lean:167` —
25	```
26	noncomputable def pullback (f : X ⟶ Y) : Y.Modules ⥤ X.Modules :=
27	  SheafOfModules.pullback f.toRingCatSheafHom
28	```
29	So the two "spellings" are **the same Mathlib declaration and its one-step δ-unfolding** — not a
30	parallel API. `Scheme.Modules.pullback f` ≡ `SheafOfModules.pullback f.toRingCatSheafHom` by a single
31	`delta`. The "parallelism" is illusory; it is a non-reducible `def` boundary, not two definitions.

34	- `Scheme.Modules` = `SheafOfModules X.ringCatSheaf` (Sheaf.lean:37, plain `def`).

37	  (`Mathlib/Algebra/Category/ModuleCat/Sheaf/PullbackContinuous.lean:53`). **This `leftAdjoint` is
38	  the real cost** — an opaque, `Lan`-built left adjoint. isDefEq over it (in either spelling) is what
39	  detonates, not the `Scheme.Modules.pullback` δ-step (that is trivial).

32	`PresheafOfModules.monoidalCategoryStruct` (and `.monoidalCategory`),
33	`Mathlib.Algebra.Category.ModuleCat.Presheaf.Monoidal`:
34	```
35	{C} → [Category C] → {R : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ CommRingCat} →
36	  MonoidalCategoryStruct (PresheafOfModules (R.comp (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)))
37	```
38	The instance is **keyed on the carrier having the syntactic shape `R ⋙ forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat`**
39	(`R.comp (forget₂ …)`), with `R : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ CommRingCat`. There is **NO** Mathlib instance keyed on
40	`Sheaf.val`/`Sheaf.obj`/`FullSubcategory.obj`. The absence is deliberate: Mathlib expects every
41	monoidal `PresheafOfModules` carrier to be carried in the `⋙ forget₂` form.
42

44	- `?carrier = X.presheaf ⋙ forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat` → discr-tree key `Functor.comp ?R (forget₂ …)`
45	  matches; unifies `R := X.presheaf`; instance fires. ✓
46	- `?carrier = Sheaf.val X.ringCatSheaf` (= `X.ringCatSheaf.obj`, the deprecated `.obj` of a
47	  `(sheafCompose _ _).obj X.sheaf`) → head is `FullSubcategory.obj`, NOT `Functor.comp`; the
48	  higher-order unification `?R.comp (forget₂ …) =?= Sheaf.val X.ringCatSheaf` is never even tried at

24	U × U --(φ_U × φ_U)--> G × G --(id × inv)--> G × G --m--> G.
25	```
26	Clearly `Φ` is defined at a diagonal point `(x, x)` if `φ` is defined at `x`, and then
27	`Φ(x, x) = e`. Conversely, if `Φ` is defined at `(x, x)`, then it is defined on an open
28	neighbourhood of `(x, x)`; in particular there is an open `U ⊆ V` such that `Φ` is defined on
29	`{x} × U`. After possibly replacing `U` by a smaller open subset (not necessarily containing `x`),
30	`φ` will be defined on `U`. For `u ∈ U`, the formula `φ(x) = Φ(x, u)·φ(u)` defines `φ` at `x`.
31	Thus **`φ` is defined at `x` iff `Φ` is defined at `(x, x)`.**
32	
33	The rational map `Φ` defines a map `Φ* : 𝒪_{G,e} → k(V × V)`. Since `Φ` sends `(x, x)` to `e` if
34	it is defined there, `Φ` is defined at `(x, x)` **iff `Im(𝒪_{G,e}) ⊆ 𝒪_{V×V,(x,x)}`.**
35	
36	Now `V × V` is nonsingular, so there is a good theory of divisors. For a nonzero rational function
37	`f` on `V × V`, write `div(f) = div(f)₀ − div(f)_∞` with both effective (`div(f)_∞ = div(f⁻¹)₀`).
38	Then
39	```
40	𝒪_{V×V,(x,x)} = { f ∈ k(V×V) | div(f)_∞ does not contain (x,x) } ∪ {0}.
41	```
42	Suppose `φ` is not defined at `x`. Then for some `f ∈ Im(φ*)`, `(x, x) ∈ div(f)_∞`, and clearly
43	`Φ` is not defined at the points `(y, y) ∈ Δ ∩ div(f)_∞`. **This is a subset of pure codimension
44	one in `Δ` (AG 9.2)**, and when we identify it with a subset of `V`, it is a subset of `V` of
45	codimension one passing through `x` on which `φ` is not defined. ∎
46

1	# Analogy: the two pullback "spellings" on `X.Modules` — parallel API or one alias?
2	
3	## Mode
4	api-alignment
5	
6	## Slug
7	pullback-spelling
8	
9	## Iteration
10	310
11	
12	## Question
13	Is `Scheme.Modules.pullback f` a needless parallel to `SheafOfModules.pullback (toRingCatSheafHom f)`?
14	What is the Mathlib-idiomatic way to make the two interchangeable at the NatTrans/whisker level
15	WITHOUT a global isDefEq blowup, and how does Mathlib prove `leftAdjointUniq`/`conjugateEquiv`
16	comparison cocycles over adjoint functors written two ways without the monolithic functor isDefEq?
17	
18	## Project artifact(s)
19	- `AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/TensorObjSubstrate.lean:2572` — `sheafificationCompPullback_comp` (D3′ S1 cocycle).
20	- `AlgebraicJacobian/Cohomology/FlatBaseChange.lean:752` — `pullbackSpecTildeNatIso` (FBC move-(2) cocycle).
21	
22	## CRITICAL CORRECTION TO THE DIRECTIVE'S PREMISE
23	`Scheme.Modules.pullback` is **NOT project-local**. It is **Mathlib**:
24	`Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Modules/Sheaf.lean:167` —
25	```
26	noncomputable def pullback (f : X ⟶ Y) : Y.Modules ⥤ X.Modules :=
27	  SheafOfModules.pullback f.toRingCatSheafHom
28	```
29	So the two "spellings" are **the same Mathlib declaration and its one-step δ-unfolding** — not a
30	parallel API. `Scheme.Modules.pullback f` ≡ `SheafOfModules.pullback f.toRingCatSheafHom` by a single
31	`delta`. The "parallelism" is illusory; it is a non-reducible `def` boundary, not two definitions.
32	
33	Supporting Mathlib facts (all `[verified]` this run):
34	- `Scheme.Modules` = `SheafOfModules X.ringCatSheaf` (Sheaf.lean:37, plain `def`).
35	- `Scheme.Hom.toRingCatSheafHom` = Mathlib, `Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Modules/Presheaf.lean:42`.
36	- `SheafOfModules.pullback φ` = `(pushforward φ).leftAdjoint`
37	  (`Mathlib/Algebra/Category/ModuleCat/Sheaf/PullbackContinuous.lean:53`). **This `leftAdjoint` is
38	  the real cost** — an opaque, `Lan`-built left adjoint. isDefEq over it (in either spelling) is what
39	  detonates, not the `Scheme.Modules.pullback` δ-step (that is trivial).
40	
41	## Decisions identified
42	
43	### Decision 1: Is `Scheme.Modules.pullback` a parallel API to align away?
44	- **Mathlib idiom**: Mathlib *itself* created `Scheme.Modules.pullback` as the higher-level alias
45	  over `SheafOfModules.pullback ∘ toRingCatSheafHom`, and re-exported the **entire cocycle API** on
46	  top of it so downstream users never touch the `SheafOfModules` spelling: `pullbackComp`
47	  (Sheaf.lean:219), `pullbackId` (199), `pullbackCongr` (235), `pullbackPushforwardAdjunction` (172),
48	  `conjugateEquiv_pullbackComp_inv` (238), `conjugateEquiv_pullbackId_hom` (203), and the full
49	  `pseudofunctor` (300) with `pseudofunctor_associativity/left_unitality/right_unitality` (246/263/277).
50	- **Project's path**: uses `Scheme.Modules.pullback` almost everywhere (correct); the mixing only
51	  happens at sheafification junctions where low-level `SheafOfModules.pullback (toRingCatSheafHom f)`
52	  leaks in via `sheafificationCompPullback`/`pullbackObjUnitToUnit`.
53	- **Gap**: identical (it IS the Mathlib idiom).
54	- **Verdict**: **PROCEED**. Keep `Scheme.Modules.pullback` as the canonical spelling; fold the
55	  low-level spelling UP to it, never the reverse.
56	
57	### Decision 2: syntactic bridge that avoids the isDefEq blowup
58	- **Mathlib idiom (primary)**: `set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in` on the
59	  lemma. Mathlib applies this knob to **every** pullback-cocycle lemma touching these `leftAdjoint`
60	  functors — Sheaf.lean:131,244,261,275,289; PullbackContinuous.lean:75; and 6 more pullback-adjacent

1	# Analogy: composition-coherence of a `leftAdjointUniq` comparison across a composite of adjunctions (one factor a reflective localization)
2	
3	## Mode
4	cross-domain-inspiration
5	
6	## Slug
7	d3recast309
8	
9	## Iteration
10	309
11	
12	## Structural problem (abstracted)
13	Two left adjoints `L_A, L_B` to the **same** right adjoint `R` over a vertical composite of
14	adjunctions (one factor a reflective localization). The canonical iso `S := leftAdjointUniq A B`
15	is a *comparison of left adjoints*. We need its **cocycle/composition coherence**: for a 2-step
16	composite `h≫f`, `S_{h≫f}` factors through `S_f` (whiskered), `S_h`, and the two pseudofunctor
17	coherences `pullbackComp` (left adjoints) / `pushforwardComp` (right adjoints). The hand
18	`homEquiv` telescope transposes the whole identity under a **single** adjunction `A_{h≫f}`, which
19	forces every comparison through one unit/counit — and the intermediate-scheme sheafification
20	`sheafAdj_Y` buried inside `A_h = sheafAdj_Y.comp ShPb_h` has nowhere to live in that single
21	transpose. It must be slid in by hand. That sliding is the wall.
22	
23	## Failed approaches (from directive)
24	- Mirror `gr_pullbackObjUnitToUnit_comp` (forward `homEquiv` telescope, `change`+`have`+`erw`):
25	  the h-comparison has no sheafification partner free in the single-adjunction transpose.
26	- Forward explicit-`have`+`erw` assembly: fragile + blows the 3.2M-heartbeat budget.
27	
28	## Key discovery (verified by LSP this iter)
29	`leftAdjointUniq` **is, definitionally, a conjugate of the identity.** Both facts are `rfl`:
30	- `(conjugateEquiv adj1 adj2).symm (𝟙 R) = (adj1.leftAdjointUniq adj2).inv`  — `rfl` (verified).
31	- `SheafOfModules.sheafificationCompPullback φ = A_φ.leftAdjointUniq B_φ`     — `rfl`
32	  (already in-file: `sheafificationCompPullback_eq_leftAdjointUniq`, L1603).
33	
34	Therefore the comparison `(sheafificationCompPullback φ).inv` **is** `conjugateEquiv A_φ B_φ`'s
35	preimage of `𝟙 R_φ`, and the whole coherence can be discharged in Mathlib's **conjugate calculus**
36	(`Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Adjunction/Mates.lean`) with NO `homEquiv` telescope.
37	
38	## Why the conjugate calculus dodges the obstruction (the core insight)
39	The `homEquiv` telescope transposes under ONE adjunction `A_{h≫f}`; every factor must be expressed
40	through that single transpose's unit/counit, so `sheafAdj_Y` (data of `A_h`, neither a factor of
41	`A_{h≫f}` nor free in the residual) has to be slid in by hand.
42	
43	`conjugateEquiv_comp` keeps each comparison as a conjugate **w.r.t. its own adjunction pair**:
44	```
45	conjugateEquiv adj₁ adj₂ α ≫ conjugateEquiv adj₂ adj₃ β = conjugateEquiv adj₁ adj₃ (β ≫ α)
46	```
47	The **middle adjunction `adj₂` is free** — it is exactly the intermediate-scheme composite
48	`A_Y / B_Y` that carries `sheafAdj_Y`. So `sheafAdj_Y` becomes a *parameter* of `adj₂`, absorbed,
49	never needing to be free in a transposed chain. This is the precise structural reason the cocycle
50	closes where the telescope stalled.
51	
52	## Analogues found
53	
54	### Analogue: `CategoryTheory.conjugateEquiv_comp` (`Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Adjunction/Mates.lean`)
55	- **Domain**: category theory / bicategory mates (the conjugate = mate with identity verticals).
56	- **Same structural problem there**: vertical stacking of conjugate transformations across THREE
57	  adjunctions `adj₁,adj₂,adj₃` (different middle), with the order-reversing fusion law above. This
58	  is `mateEquiv_vcomp` specialized to identity verticals (`G=H=𝟙`); see also

9	## Milne's statement (Abelian Varieties, §I.3 Lemma 3.3, p. 17)
10	
11	> Let `φ : V ⇢ G` be a rational map from a nonsingular variety to a group variety. Then either
12	> `φ` is defined on all of `V`, or the points where it is not defined form a closed subset of
13	> pure codimension 1 in `V` (i.e., a finite union of prime divisors).
14	
15	Combined with Milne 3.1 (`indeterminacy_codimGe2_of_smooth_of_complete`, codim ≥ 2 into a complete
16	target — **proved**), for an abelian-variety target this forces `Z(φ) = ∅`
17	(`av_indeterminacyLocus_eq_empty`), hence extension (Milne 3.2).
18	
19	## Milne's proof (transcribed verbatim from the PDF, pages 23–24)
20	
21	Define a rational map `Φ : V × V ⇢ G`, `(x, y) ↦ φ(x)·φ(y)⁻¹`. More precisely, if `(U, φ_U)`
22	represents `φ`, then `Φ` is represented by
23	```
24	U × U --(φ_U × φ_U)--> G × G --(id × inv)--> G × G --m--> G.
25	```
26	Clearly `Φ` is defined at a diagonal point `(x, x)` if `φ` is defined at `x`, and then
27	`Φ(x, x) = e`. Conversely, if `Φ` is defined at `(x, x)`, then it is defined on an open
28	neighbourhood of `(x, x)`; in particular there is an open `U ⊆ V` such that `Φ` is defined on
29	`{x} × U`. After possibly replacing `U` by a smaller open subset (not necessarily containing `x`),
30	`φ` will be defined on `U`. For `u ∈ U`, the formula `φ(x) = Φ(x, u)·φ(u)` defines `φ` at `x`.
31	Thus **`φ` is defined at `x` iff `Φ` is defined at `(x, x)`.**
32	
33	The rational map `Φ` defines a map `Φ* : 𝒪_{G,e} → k(V × V)`. Since `Φ` sends `(x, x)` to `e` if
34	it is defined there, `Φ` is defined at `(x, x)` **iff `Im(𝒪_{G,e}) ⊆ 𝒪_{V×V,(x,x)}`.**
35	
36	Now `V × V` is nonsingular, so there is a good theory of divisors. For a nonzero rational function
37	`f` on `V × V`, write `div(f) = div(f)₀ − div(f)_∞` with both effective (`div(f)_∞ = div(f⁻¹)₀`).
38	Then
39	```
40	𝒪_{V×V,(x,x)} = { f ∈ k(V×V) | div(f)_∞ does not contain (x,x) } ∪ {0}.
41	```
42	Suppose `φ` is not defined at `x`. Then for some `f ∈ Im(φ*)`, `(x, x) ∈ div(f)_∞`, and clearly
43	`Φ` is not defined at the points `(y, y) ∈ Δ ∩ div(f)_∞`. **This is a subset of pure codimension
44	one in `Δ` (AG 9.2)**, and when we identify it with a subset of `V`, it is a subset of `V` of
45	codimension one passing through `x` on which `φ` is not defined. ∎

**Estimate: ~60% of `analogies/` is retire-able (~74 of 123), leaving ~49 keeps.** In my sample the ratio was 5/15 retire, but the sample deliberately over-weighted the recent 304–329 cohort (which is almost all keep) and the large topical surveys; the bulk mid-range is worse.

Three cheap, mechanical discriminators, in decreasing strength:

**(A) Deleted-lane grep — 47 files, near-certain RETIRE (38% of the directory on its own).**
